harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1 (Alpine 3.23), added fstab tmpfs entries for /tmp and /dev/shm with noexec,nosuid,nodev,relatime and mounted them live. Verified functionally (script execution blocked, setuid bit ignored, device node access denied) both before and after a full node reboot, confirming persistence.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline state: OS release, /etc/fstab, and current mounts for /tmp and /dev/shm
Backed up /etc/fstab and appended tmpfs entries for /tmp and /dev/shm with rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime options
Mounted a fresh tmpfs on /tmp (previously part of root ext4) and remounted /dev/shm with the new options

Ran functional checks: attempted to execute a script from /tmp and /dev/shm (denied), set setuid bit on a binary in /tmp (bit ignored at execution), created and wrote to a device node in /tmp (denied)
Captured baseline boot_id and uptime, then triggered a reboot via 'sudo -n reboot' backgrounded so the exec call could return before disconnection
Polled node1 until it became reachable again and confirmed a new boot_id/reset uptime, proving an actual restart occurred

Re-verified after reboot: fstab entries intact, findmnt shows tmpfs with noexec,nosuid,nodev active on both /tmp and /dev/shm, and repeated the exec/setuid/device-node functional tests, all confirming enforcement persisted
Cleaned up all test artifacts (exectest.sh, busybox_suid, nulltest device node)

evidence.requirement: Baseline healthy state before restart (fstab config, mount options, functional enforcement)
evidence.summary: Confirmed initial state (no tmpfs entries for /tmp), then added fstab entries, remounted /tmp and /dev/shm as tmpfs with noexec,nosuid,nodev, and ran functional tests proving execution, setuid, and device node use are blocked on both.
Backgrounded 'sudo -n reboot' returned acknowledgement, and the immediate next poll showed connection reset, confirming the restart was issued and the node went down.

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving an actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from e5ad1dea-7ce9-4e34-8458-f4df4867e01e (baseline, uptime 55s) to 7cb7bd3a-1412-45ef-8c63-09e9bfb67769 (post-reboot, uptime 15s), proving a genuine reboot rather than a service restart.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of mount hardening and fstab persistence
evidence.summary: After reboot, /etc/fstab still contains the tmpfs entries, findmnt confirms noexec,nosuid,nodev active on both /tmp and /dev/shm, and repeated functional tests confirm script execution, setuid, and device node access are all still blocked.
